from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "A basis is a set of building blocks.",
            "Meet Bob. He uses unit vectors i and j.",
            "To reach (3, 2), he takes 5 total steps."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Check: The Standard Home", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define origin point to ensure (3,2) stays within the right-side grid area
        origin_point = self.grid["E2"] 

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create a standard square grid
        grid_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 5, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": "#333333",
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.6
            },
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_color": "#555555"}
        ).move_to(origin_point + 2*RIGHT + 1.5*UP)
        
        self.play(Create(grid_plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Vector i (blue)
        i_vec = Arrow(origin_point, origin_point + RIGHT, buff=0, color="#0000FF")
        # Fixed: Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' executable dependency
        i_label = Text("i", color="#0000FF", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        i_label.next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Vector j (red)
        j_vec = Arrow(origin_point, origin_point + UP, buff=0, color="#FF0000")
        # Fixed: Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' executable dependency
        j_label = Text("j", color="#FF0000", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        j_label.next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Bob initial position (origin)
        bob = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.1)
        bob.move_to(origin_point)
        bob_label = Text("Bob", font_size=16, color=YELLOW).next_to(bob, DL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_vec),
            Write(i_label),
            GrowArrow(j_vec),
            Write(j_label),
            FadeIn(bob),
            Write(bob_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Target point (3, 2)
        target_point = origin_point + 3 * RIGHT + 2 * UP
        
        # Path trace
        path_x = Line(origin_point, origin_point + 3 * RIGHT, color=BLUE, stroke_width=3)
        path_y = Line(origin_point + 3 * RIGHT, target_point, color=RED, stroke_width=3)
        
        # Target markers
        target_dot = Dot(target_point, color=YELLOW, radius=0.08)
        # Fixed: Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' executable dependency
        coord_label = Text("(3, 2)", font_size=28, color=YELLOW).next_to(target_dot, UR, buff=0.1)

        # Bob's movement: 3 steps along i then 2 along j
        self.play(
            bob.animate.move_to(origin_point + 3 * RIGHT),
            bob_label.animate.move_to(origin_point + 3 * RIGHT + DOWN * 0.3),
            Create(path_x),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.play(
            bob.animate.move_to(target_point),
            bob_label.animate.move_to(target_point + UP * 0.3),
            Create(path_y),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(target_dot),
            Write(coord_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup Title and Lecture Lines
        title_txt = "The Perspective Shift: Enter the Robot"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Meet Z-4. His world is tilted 45 degrees.', 
            'He sees the same point using different basis vectors.', 
            'His coordinates describe the same location in his language.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_txt, lecture_lines)

        # Color definitions
        Z4_COLOR = "#00FF00"   # Green
        B1_COLOR = "#00FF00"   # Green
        B2_COLOR = "#FFFF00"   # Yellow
        STAR_COLOR = "#FFD700" # Gold
        BOB_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight line 1 color
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(Z4_COLOR))

        # Create Z-4 Robot Icon at B2
        z4_body = Square(side_length=0.6, color=Z4_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.3)
        z4_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.04, color=Z4_COLOR).shift(LEFT*0.12 + UP*0.1)
        z4_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.04, color=Z4_COLOR).shift(RIGHT*0.12 + UP*0.1)
        z4_mouth = Line(LEFT*0.1, RIGHT*0.1, color=Z4_COLOR).shift(DOWN*0.15)
        z4_robot = VGroup(z4_body, z4_eye_l, z4_eye_r, z4_mouth).rotate(PI/4)
        self.place_at_grid(z4_robot, "B2")

        # Bob's coordinate system (standard grid) centered at D3
        bob_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY_E, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_at_grid(bob_plane, "D3")

        # Z-4's Tilted Basis Vectors
        origin_coords = self.grid["D3"]
        b1_target = self.grid["C4"]
        b2_target = self.grid["C2"]

        b1_vec = Arrow(origin_coords, b1_target, buff=0, color=B1_COLOR)
        b2_vec = Arrow(origin_coords, b2_target, buff=0, color=B2_COLOR)
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid latex dependency error
        b1_label = Text("b1", color=B1_COLOR, font_size=22)
        b1_label.next_to(b1_target, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        b2_label = Text("b2", color=B2_COLOR, font_size=22)
        b2_label.next_to(b2_target, UL, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(bob_plane))
        self.play(FadeIn(z4_robot, shift=DOWN))
        self.play(
            Create(b1_vec), 
            Create(b2_vec), 
            Write(b1_label), 
            Write(b2_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight line 2 color
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(B2_COLOR))

        # Gold star at Bob's (1,1) which corresponds to grid position C4
        star = Star(n=5, color=STAR_COLOR, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(star, "C4", scale_factor=0.2)
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid latex dependency error
        bob_label = Text("(1, 1) Bob", color=BOB_COLOR, font_size=22)
        bob_label.next_to(self.grid["C4"], RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(star, scale=0.5))
        self.play(Write(bob_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight line 3 color
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(STAR_COLOR))

        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid latex dependency error
        z4_label = Text("(1, 0) Z-4", color=Z4_COLOR, font_size=22)
        z4_label.next_to(self.grid["C4"], UP, buff=0.2)

        # Visual indicator: highlighting the basis vector b1 as the axis of measurement
        focus_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=Z4_COLOR).move_to(self.grid["C4"])

        self.play(Create(focus_circle))
        self.play(Write(z4_label))
        self.play(Indicate(z4_label, color=Z4_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeOut(focus_circle))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration for Section 3
        title = "Section 3: The Transformation Matrix"
        lecture = [
            "- Mapping basis vectors",
            "- Matrix columns = new basis",
            "- Transforming a vector v",
            "- Av = the new coordinates"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture)

        # Create Coordinate System in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"stroke_width": 2},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3}
        )
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "C4")
        
        # Standard basis vectors
        origin = plane.get_origin()
        i_hat = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(1, 0) - origin, color=GREEN).shift(origin)
        j_hat = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(0, 1) - origin, color=RED).shift(origin)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_label = Text("i", color=GREEN, font_size=20, slant=ITALIC).next_to(i_hat, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", color=RED, font_size=20, slant=ITALIC).next_to(j_hat, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Transformed basis vectors (Example: Shear/Rotation)
        new_i = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(1, 0.5) - origin, color=YELLOW).shift(origin)
        new_j = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(0.5, 1) - origin, color=ORANGE).shift(origin)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        matrix = Text(
            "A = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]", 
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix, "F4")

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(i_hat, new_i),
            Transform(j_hat, new_j),
            FadeOut(i_label),
            FadeOut(j_label),
            Write(matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration
        COLOR_FLOW = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_CAMERA = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_APP = "#FFD700"    # Gold
        
        lines = [
            'Basis, Matrix, Transformation: that is the core flow.',
            'This math powers camera rotations in video games.',
            'Change of basis helps find patterns in complex data.'
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Visual Summary & Application", lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Flow diagram: Basis -> Matrix P -> Transformation
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_FLOW))
        
        basis_rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        basis_text = Text("Basis", font_size=20, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        basis_grp = VGroup(basis_rect, basis_text)
        self.place_at_grid(basis_grp, "B1", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        matrix_rect = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        matrix_text = Text("Matrix P", font_size=20, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        matrix_grp = VGroup(matrix_rect, matrix_text)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_grp, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        trans_rect = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=0.8, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        trans_text = Text("Transformation", font_size=18, color=COLOR_FLOW)
        trans_grp = VGroup(trans_rect, trans_text)
        self.place_at_grid(trans_grp, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=basis_grp.get_right(), end=matrix_grp.get_left(), color=COLOR_FLOW, buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=matrix_grp.get_right(), end=trans_grp.get_left(), color=COLOR_FLOW, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(basis_grp),
            Create(arrow1),
            FadeIn(matrix_grp),
            Create(arrow2),
            FadeIn(trans_grp)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a 2D camera icon rotating to show a basis change
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_CAMERA)
        )
        
        # Simple camera icon
        cam_body = Rectangle(width=1.0, height=0.6, color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=0.3)
        cam_lens = Triangle(color=COLOR_CAMERA, fill_opacity=0.5).scale(0.2).rotate(-PI/2)
        cam_lens.next_to(cam_body, RIGHT, buff=0)
        
        # Local Basis Vectors for Camera
        v1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.8, color=RED, buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.8, color=GREEN, buff=0)
        camera_basis = VGroup(v1, v2)
        
        camera_system = VGroup(cam_body, cam_lens, camera_basis)
        self.place_in_area(camera_system, "D1", "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(camera_system))
        self.play(camera_system.animate.rotate(45 * DEGREES), run_time=2)
        self.play(camera_system.animate.rotate(-90 * DEGREES), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show Bob and Z-4 together at the gold star's location
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_APP)
        )
        
        # Character Placeholders (as no specific assets provided in path format)
        star = Star(n=5, color=COLOR_APP, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(star, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Bob (Circle for head, line for body)
        bob = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE), Line(DOWN*0.15, DOWN*0.5, color=WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(bob, "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        bob_label = Text("Bob", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(bob, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Z-4 (Square for head, square for body)
        z4 = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.2, color=WHITE), Square(side_length=0.3, color=WHITE).next_to(ORIGIN, DOWN, buff=0))
        self.place_at_grid(z4, "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        z4_label = Text("Z-4", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(z4, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(star),
            FadeIn(bob), FadeIn(bob_label),
            FadeIn(z4), FadeIn(z4_label)
        )
        
        # Final Move: characters move to focus on the star
        self.play(
            bob.animate.move_to(self.grid["F4"] + LEFT*0.3),
            bob_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["F4"] + LEFT*0.3 + UP*0.4),
            z4.animate.move_to(self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT*0.3),
            z4_label.animate.move_to(self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT*0.3 + UP*0.4),
            star.animate.scale(1.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: Seeing the World Through Different Eyes

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: The Standard Home
sections.content: Briefly review that a 'Basis' is a set of building blocks (vectors) used to reach any point in space. Focus on the Standard Basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1). Visualize a character, 'Bob', standing on a standard square grid.
sections.example: Bob wants to reach point (3, 2). He takes 3 steps along the i-axis and 2 steps along the j-axis. This is his 'language'.

sections.title: The Perspective Shift: Enter the Robot
sections.content: Introduce a new character, 'Z-4 the Robot', who is rotated 45 degrees. Z-4 has his own basis vectors, B1 and B2, which are diagonal relative to Bob's grid. Explain that while they look at the same physical point, they use different numbers to describe it.
sections.example: A gold star is placed in the room. Bob says it's at (1, 1). Z-4, using his diagonal axes, says it's just '1 unit forward' on his primary axis (1, 0) in his language.

sections.title: The Bridge: The Transition Matrix (P)
sections.content: Define the Change of Basis Matrix (P) as a 'translator'. To build P, we express Z-4's basis vectors using Bob's coordinates. Each column of the matrix P is one of Z-4’s basis vectors written in Bob’s language.
sections.example: If Z-4's first basis vector B1 is (1, 1) in Bob's world and B2 is (-1, 1), the matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]]. This matrix is the dictionary between them.

sections.title: The Calculation: Translating Coordinates
sections.content: Introduce the core formula: [x]_Bob = P * [x]_Z-4. Explain that multiplying Z-4's coordinates by P 'stretches and rotates' them back into Bob's standard grid view. Use a split-screen animation showing the vector moving from the tilted grid to the square grid.
sections.example: If Z-4 says a point is at (1, 0) in his world, we multiply P by [1, 0] to get Bob's coordinates: [[1, -1], [1, 1]] * [1, 0] = (1, 1). It matches!

sections.title: Inverse Thinking: Bob to Z-4
sections.content: What if Bob wants to talk to Z-4? Introduce the Inverse Matrix (P⁻¹). Explain that if P takes us from Z-4 to Bob, P⁻¹ takes us from Bob back to Z-4. Visualize the grid 'un-warping'.
sections.example: Bob has a point (0, 2). He uses P⁻¹ to tell Z-4 that the point is actually at (1, 1) in Z-4's coordinate system.

sections.title: Visual Summary & Application
sections.content: Summarize the flow: Basis -> Transition Matrix -> Coordinate Transformation. Mention real-world applications like computer graphics (camera angles) and data compression (changing basis to find patterns).
sections.example: Think of a video game camera: as the camera rotates, the 'basis' of the screen changes, but the 3D world stays the same. Change of basis math keeps the player aligned with the world.
